title: CHAPTER 10: GOVERNMENT SCHEMES OF ANDHRA PRADESH

blocks.content: Andhra Pradesh has been at the forefront of implementing welfare schemes and development programs. The following schemes are important from an examination perspective.

cells: Financial assistance of Rs. 15,000/year to mothers to send children to school; also covers grandparents of girl students; Direct Benefit Transfer
100% reimbursement of tuition fees for SC/ST/BC/minority students in higher education; covers private colleges
Monthly living expenses (hostel charges) for SC/ST/BC/minority students in higher education
Extension and enhancement of Amma Vodi scheme
Enhanced state extension of the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (Ayushman Bharat); free healthcare up to Rs. 5 lakh per family
Monthly pension of Rs. 2,750–Rs. 5,000 for various categories including old age, disabled, widow, Dappu artists, fishermen, weavers, toddy tappers
2BHK housing for poor families; construction of 25+ lakh houses
Rs. 13,500 per year to farmers (including tenant farmers); complements PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi
Zero-interest loans to farmers for short-term agricultural operations
Financial assistance to BC, SC, ST, Minority women aged 45-60 for self-employment; Rs. 18,750/year for 4 years
Financial support of Rs. 24,000/year to handloom weavers
Financial support of Rs. 15,000/year to EBC (Economically Backward Classes) widows and others
Fast-track courts for heinous crimes against women; death penalty for gang rape
AP's accident insurance and life insurance scheme
Setting up secretariats at village/ward level for delivering governance at doorstep
Village governance system with multi-function employees for welfare delivery
Combination of several educational welfare schemes under 'Navaratnalu'
Physical infrastructure improvement of all government schools; benches, fans, toilets, drinking water, electricity, compound walls, playgrounds
Mid-day meal scheme; nutritious eggs, milk, bananas provided to school children
Broadband connectivity to all households and institutions in AP at affordable rates
Major irrigation project launched 2004; aimed at completing 86 irrigation projects
Loan at 3% interest to farmers (paddy at 1 paisa per rupee = Pavala Vaddi)
Free LPG connection to poor families (precursor to PM Ujjwala)
Subsidized meals at Rs. 5/Rs. 10; renamed under YSR government as Annapurna Canteens
TDP's IT-driven governance; Chandrababu Naidu known as 'CEO of AP'
TDP's long-term vision document for AP development

Super Six Guarantees – Thalliki Vandanam (Rs. 15,000 to mothers), Yuva Vikasam (skills for unemployed youth), Anna Canteens revival, Deepam 2.0 (3 free LPG cylinders/year), Riddi (Rs. 1,500/month to women), Agri support

blocks.content: 10.3 Central Schemes with Special Importance to AP

cells: National Project status; across Godavari; major irrigation and drinking water project; construction ongoing
Special status demands; revenue deficit grants; backwardness grants for Rayalaseema and Uttarandhra
Part of DMIC network; major industrial development initiative
AP massive housing implementation; joint with state Navaratnalu housing scheme
Visakhapatnam and Kakinada selected as Smart Cities
